presentingComplaint: Sudden onset severe breathlessness and chest heaviness 6 hours ago, now cold, clammy and confused.
history: A 64-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes was brought to the emergency department after 6 hours of central chest heaviness radiating to the left arm, associated with diaphoresis and nausea. He delayed seeking care. Over the last 2 hours he has become progressively breathless, drowsy, and his family noted his hands and feet turning cold and mottled. He has not passed urine since arrival. No prior history of MI; he is on amlodipine and metformin only, no antiplatelet or statin. No fever, no diarrhea/vomiting preceding the episode, no history of recent large-volume fluid loss.
examination: Anxious but obtunded, responding only to voice (GCS 13). Cold, clammy, mottled peripheries with delayed capillary refill (>4 seconds). Raised JVP. Bilateral basal crackles two-thirds up both lung fields. Soft new pansystolic murmur at the apex not present on old records, raising concern for acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle involvement. Heart sounds soft with a gallop rhythm; no pericardial rub. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. No peripheral edema yet (acute presentation). Urinary catheter placed in ED draining minimal concentrated urine.
imaging: 12-lead ECG: ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4 with reciprocal inferior depression, consistent with acute anterior STEMI
Portable CXR: pulmonary venous congestion with bilateral perihilar haziness, no pneumothorax

Bedside echocardiogram: severe global and anteroapical hypokinesis, LVEF ~25%, moderate-severe functional/ischemic mitral regurgitation, no pericardial effusion, no mechanical complication (no VSD) identified on initial scan
Coronary angiography (emergent): proximal LAD 100% occlusion; culprit lesion
differentialDiagnoses: Cardiogenic shock secondary to acute anterior STEMI (post-MI pump failure)
Acute mechanical complication of MI (papillary muscle rupture / VSD)
finalDiagnosis: Cardiogenic shock due to acute anterior STEMI (post-MI pump failure) with secondary ischemic mitral regurgitation

contraindications: Avoid excessive IV fluid boluses given pulmonary edema; use cautious, small aliquots only if clearly volume-responsive
Beta-blockers contraindicated acutely in overt cardiogenic shock
Caution with nitrates given hypotension — avoid until shock reversed
Metformin should be held given AKI and shock (risk of lactic acidosis)
edgeCases: If mechanical complication (VSD or papillary muscle rupture) is confirmed, urgent cardiac surgery referral supersedes standard PCI-only pathway
Right ventricular infarction can mimic/complicate presentation and changes fluid management (may require preload support rather than restriction) — right-sided ECG leads should be checked
In elderly or frail patients, decisions about mechanical circulatory support (IABP/Impella/ECMO) require goals-of-care discussion
cardiogenic_shock is not a bacterial/infective diagnosis, so no antimicrobial stewardship tier applies (stewardship = null); do not force a septic-shock antibiotic pathway
expectedMaiK: MaiK should flag this as cardiogenic shock post-STEMI (not septic shock) given the temporal link to acute chest pain, ECG changes, and echo-confirmed severe LV dysfunction; commentary should recommend urgent reperfusion (primary PCI), inotrope/vasopressor support (e.g., norepinephrine first-line per ESC/AHA), avoidance of large fluid boluses, and consideration of mechanical circulatory support if refractory, while explicitly noting no antibiotics are indicated absent infective source.
